name: green-zone-text-values-compact
note: plotzone text= interpolating an AUTHOR-supplied value with the `compact` format. The template mechanism already sampled node ids at spawn; what was restricted is WHICH nodes could fill a slot -- only the output's own geometry (`{top}`/`{bottom}`), never an arbitrary series. `text_value=` lifts that, which is what the Pine's `EQH (8.8M)` needs, where 8.8M is the SUM OF TWO PIVOT VOLUMES and has nothing to do with the box's own edges. `compact` is load-bearing rather than sugar: Pine builds the magnitude suffix with an if/else returning different STRINGS per magnitude, and this language has no string series, so the suffix has to live in the formatter. Here the zone spawns at bar 2 with volume 6_100_000, so the text must read exactly `EQH (6.1M)`. `text_value=` is SINGULAR on purpose. An array literal would have been the obvious spelling, but OS1011 bans collection literals in v1 and the spawn-sampled-values design itself declines arrays (they are the imperative object model this language does not want). Every label in scope needs exactly one value, so a single argument is the honest surface; a second value would be a named sibling, never a list.
source:
indicator("H", shorttitle="H", overlay=true)
plotzone(bar_index == 2, high, low, "EQH", extend=extend.bars, bars=1, text="EQH ({0:compact})", text_value=volume)
